 This appeal coming on for order this day, the court passed the
following:
 Order

This appeal by the appellants/claimants u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 08.08.2018 passed by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District-Mandsaur in Claim Case No.700228/2016 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and findings recorded by the claims tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the claims tribunal, in the case of death of Sanjay Kumar, claims tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.24,32,584/- in favour of the claimants/appellants with interest from filing of claim petition till realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants contended that compensation awarded by the tribunal accepting earning of the deceased as Rs.15000/- per month is inadequate looking to the fact that he was working as an advocate.
He was leading practitioner having car and was having his junior advocates.
Children of the deceased were going in school and the deceased paid near about Rs.80,000/- per year in the education of his children.
He deposited premium of LIC so his income must be assessed as --3-- Rs.25,000/- per month which is just and proper.
He seeks future prospects by applying adequate multiplier and prays that a reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company contended that claims tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the claims tribunal.

6. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record of the case, it is undisputed that deceased was practicing advocate in civil suit in Mandsaur and according to evidence adduced by the claimants, deceased has 3 children they are going in private school and deceased paid Rs.80,000/- per year in his education and deceased had LIC policy and paid premium of Rs.28000/- and having a car and motorcycle.

So considering these facts, in the considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper income of the deceased in the present case would be Rs.18000/-
Smt Tarasingh vs Jahangir Khan on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33890725/
2 per month.
7.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, the compensation amount deserves to be enhanced.

Hence,
the break-up of enhancement in the compensation amount is as under:-
Heads Calculation of Amount Loss of dependency Income taken Rs.18000+4500 (25% future prospects)= Rs.22,500/- p.m. X 12= Rs.2,70,000/- per annum X 14 (multiplier)=37,80,000/-
After deducting 1/4th amount (Rs.9,45,000) towards personal expenses

, the amount comes to Rs.28,35,000/-
Loss of consortium Rs.1,60,000/-
 Funeral Expenses Rs.15000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs.15000/-

Total amount :Rs.30,25,000/-
 --4--

Total amount : Rs.30,25,000/-
 MACT awarded : Rs.24,32,584/-
Enhanced amount in the present appeal: Rs.5,92,416/-
8.
Keeping in view the aforesaid, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced from Rs.24,32,584 /- to Rs.30,25,000/- with interest as fixed by the tribunal over and above the amount already awarded by the tribunal.

Hence,
the total amount enhanced in this appeal is Rs.5,92,416/- (Rs.30,25,000-24,32,584).

Accordingly,
the appellants shall be entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs. 5,92,416/- over and and above the amount which has already been awarded by the tribunal.
All other findings recorded by the tribunal shall remain intact.
The present appeal stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH)
